title: Defining relative clauses
titleVi: Mệnh đề quan hệ xác định
summary: who/which/that, khi nào bỏ được đại từ quan hệ, và cách rút gọn mệnh đề thành cụm -ing/-ed.
whyItMatters: Mệnh đề quan hệ là công cụ chính để viết câu phức — điều kiện bắt buộc để đạt band 7 ở tiêu chí Grammatical Range. Nhưng người Việt thường mắc hai lỗi hệ thống: dùng *which* cho người và giữ lại đại từ tân ngữ (*the book which I bought it*). Cả hai đều rất dễ thấy và xuất hiện ở mọi đoạn văn.

sections.heading: who, which, that: the basic choice
body: **who** for people, **which** for things, **that** for both — but *that* only in **defining** clauses (the ones without commas). *The scientist who discovered penicillin...*, *The policy which was introduced in 2015...*

The relative pronoun replaces a noun that would otherwise be repeated: *the student who won the prize* (not *the student who he won*). This double-subject error is the most common relative-clause mistake among Vietnamese speakers.
**whose** shows possession and works for people and things: *a researcher whose work changed the field*, *a city whose population is falling*.

rows: The tutor who marked my essay was strict.
The tutor (who) I asked was helpful.
The scheme that failed was expensive.
The scheme (which) they cancelled was costly.
Students whose fees are unpaid cannot enrol.
The district where I grew up has changed.
The year when the ban started was 2019.
The reason why people move is housing costs.

sections.heading: When you can drop the pronoun
body: If the relative pronoun is the **object** of the clause, it can be left out: *the book (which) I bought*, *the man (who) we met*, *the results (that) they published*.

If it is the **subject**, it cannot be dropped: *the man who lives next door* — *the man lives next door* would create a second main verb. Vietnamese allows *người đàn ông sống cạnh nhà* with nothing in between, which is exactly why learners delete the subject pronoun.
The test: look at what follows the noun. If a verb follows immediately, you need a subject pronoun. If a subject follows, the pronoun is optional.

examples.right: The article I read yesterday was convincing.
examples.note: Object pronoun omitted — correct and natural.

examples.right: The article which appeared yesterday was convincing.
examples.wrong: The article appeared yesterday was convincing.

examples.right: The people who were surveyed came from five provinces.
examples.wrong: The people were surveyed came from five provinces.
examples.note: Bị động: *who were surveyed* — không bỏ được *who*.

sections.heading: Prepositions and whom
body: In formal writing the preposition can move to the front with **whom**: *the official to whom the report was addressed*, *the method by which the data were analysed*. This is the register of academic papers.

In neutral writing, keep the preposition at the end and use *who/that* or nothing: *the official who the report was addressed to*, *the method that the data were analysed by*. Both are grammatical; mixing them (*the official to who...*) is not.
**whom** is obligatory only after a preposition in formal style. Elsewhere it is optional and increasingly rare: *the candidate whom we interviewed* is correct but *who* is also accepted.

rows: the person to whom I spoke
the report on which the decision was based
the report the decision was based on
the extent to which costs matter
the committee by whom the rules were drafted
the committee that drafted the rules

sections.heading: where, when, why — and the traps
body: **where** replaces a place expression: *the city where I was born* (= *in which*). It cannot replace an object: *the city which I visited* — not *the city where I visited*.
**when** replaces a time expression: *the decade when manufacturing collapsed*. **why** follows *reason*: *the reason why* or simply *the reason* + clause.

Note the fixed pairs: *the day when*, *the year when*, *the moment when*, *the place where*, *the reason why*. Using *that* in place of *where* is acceptable in informal English (*the place that I grew up*) but *where* is clearer.

examples.right: This is the town where my parents met.
This is the town which I visited last summer.
examples.wrong: This is the town where I visited last summer.
examples.note: *visit* cần tân ngữ, nên dùng **which**, không dùng *where*.

examples.right: The reason why enrolment fell is unclear.

sections.heading: Reducing the clause: -ing, -ed and to-infinitive
body: Defining clauses can usually be shortened, and the short version sounds more academic. Active clause → **-ing**: *students who study abroad* → *students studying abroad*. Passive clause → **-ed**: *the data which were collected in 2020* → *the data collected in 2020*.
Purpose and necessity clauses reduce to the infinitive: *the first person who arrived* → *the first person to arrive*; *there is nothing that we can do* → *there is nothing to do*.

These reductions are what make band-8 sentences compact. Compare: *The survey, which was conducted in 2021, involved 400 households* with *The 2021 survey involved 400 households* — the second is shorter and stronger, and the shortening comes from exactly this machinery.

rows: the workers who were made redundant
the first country that banned the practice
the first country to ban the practice

commonMistakes.wrong: The man which lives next door is a doctor.
commonMistakes.right: The man who lives next door is a doctor.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt dùng *người mà* cho cả người và vật, nên người học chọn *which*. Với người phải dùng **who** (hoặc *that* trong mệnh đề xác định).

commonMistakes.wrong: The book which I bought it was expensive.
commonMistakes.right: The book which I bought was expensive.
commonMistakes.why: Đại từ quan hệ **đã thay cho tân ngữ**, nên không lặp lại *it*. Đây là lỗi thừa tân ngữ điển hình của người Việt.

commonMistakes.wrong: The research published last year was influential.
commonMistakes.right: The research which was published last year was influential.
commonMistakes.why: Câu gốc thực ra đúng nếu hiểu là mệnh đề rút gọn. Lỗi nằm ở chiều ngược lại: khi cần mệnh đề đầy đủ mà bỏ đại từ **chủ ngữ** — *The research was published last year was influential* mới là sai, vì thiếu chủ ngữ cho động từ thứ hai.

commonMistakes.wrong: This is the city where I visited last summer.
commonMistakes.right: This is the city which I visited last summer.
commonMistakes.why: **where** thay cho cụm trạng ngữ chỉ nơi chốn (*in the city*), không thay cho tân ngữ. *Visit* cần tân ngữ nên phải dùng **which/that**.

commonMistakes.wrong: The reason because people migrate is economic.
commonMistakes.right: The reason why people migrate is economic.
commonMistakes.why: Tiếng Việt *lý do vì* khiến người học dùng *because*. Trong mệnh đề quan hệ chỉ lý do, đại từ là **why** (hoặc bỏ hẳn: *the reason people migrate*).

ieltsTips: Rút gọn mệnh đề quan hệ để câu gọn và học thuật hơn: `students studying abroad`, `the data collected in 2020`.
Dùng `the extent to which`, `the degree to which`, `the way in which` — ba cụm Band 8 thay cho *how* trong câu phức.
Trong Task 1, tránh chuỗi mệnh đề quan hệ dài; chuyển sang cụm danh từ: `the 2020 figure` thay cho `the figure which was recorded in 2020`.
Kiểm tra mỗi mệnh đề quan hệ có đúng một chủ ngữ: nếu đại từ quan hệ là tân ngữ, không thêm *it/them*.

exercises.question: The scientist ___ discovered the vaccine received the prize.
The report ___ was leaked to the press caused a scandal.
The students ___ fees are unpaid cannot sit the exam.
This is the village ___ my grandparents were born.
exercises.explanation: Nơi chốn, động từ *be born* không cần tân ngữ → **where**.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The film which I watched it was boring.
The film which I watched was boring.
The film who I watched was boring.
The film where I watched was boring.
exercises.explanation: Đại từ quan hệ thay tân ngữ nên không lặp *it*; vật dùng **which**.

exercises.question: The people ___ were interviewed came from five provinces.
The data ___ (collect) in 2020 showed a clear decline.
exercises.explanation: Mệnh đề bị động rút gọn: *the data collected in 2020*.

exercises.question: She was the first person ___ (arrive) at the venue.
The reason ___ so many graduates emigrate is unclear.
This is the method ___ which the samples were tested.
exercises.explanation: Cấu trúc trang trọng **by which** (tested by a method).
